hypotheses.statement: The checkout API 5xx spike was caused by an expired certificate on payments-gateway.internal, not by the checkout-api release
The temporal proximity of the release (09:09:52Z) to the incident start (09:11:47Z) led responders to incorrectly attribute the incident to the release
The recovery at 09:57:55Z was due to certificate rotation taking effect, not due to the rollback which completed later at 10:04:18Z

observed_facts.statement: The payments-gateway.internal leaf certificate expired at 09:11:40Z
Payments connector TLS handshake failures to payments-gateway.internal:8443 began at 09:11:47Z with error 'certificate verify failed: certificate has expired'
POST /v2/checkout/submit started returning 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted 3 retries, correlated with TLS failures
Alert checkout-api-error-ratio fired at 09:12:03Z with 5xx ratio 0.184 against objective 0.005 for POST /v2/checkout/submit
Alert checkout-api-latency fired at 09:14:41Z with p99 latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit rising to 10400ms (client timeout ceiling)
Release 2026.5.14-a deployed at 09:09:52Z contained only copy edits to email templates and a CSV export library dependency bump
No code path in release 2026.5.14-a is reachable from POST /v2/checkout/submit
Payments connector TLS handshakes recovered at 09:57:55Z
The 5xx ratio returned to 0.004 at 09:58:10Z, six minutes before rollback completed

open_questions.missing_evidence: Documentation or runbook identifying the team responsible for certificate renewal automation
open_questions.question: Who owns the renewal automation for the payments-gateway.internal certificate?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Incident response documentation or process records showing impact assessment
open_questions.question: Why was no customer-impact estimate recorded during the incident?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Explanation for the discrepancy between observed recovery time and documented resolution
open_questions.question: Why does the resolution note attribute recovery to rollback when evidence shows recovery occurred before rollback completion?

summary: Checkout API experienced a 5xx spike from 09:12:03Z to 09:58:10Z due to an expired certificate on payments-gateway.internal. The incident began with TLS handshake failures at 09:11:47Z, causing POST /v2/checkout/submit to return 502 errors. Recovery occurred at 09:57:55Z after certificate rotation took effect. A coincidental release at 09:09:52Z was initially blamed but contained no changes affecting the failing code path.

timeline.statement: checkout-api release 2026.5.14-a: Release 2026.5.14-a deployed to production at 09:09:52Z, two minutes and eleven seconds before alert-4471 fired. Changes: copy edits to three checkout confirmation email templates, and a dependency bump of the CSV export library used by the nightly reconciliation job. No code path in this release is reachable from POST /v2/checkout/submit.

payments connector TLS handshake failures begin: checkout-api payments-connector: repeated outbound TLS handshake failures to payments-gateway.internal:8443. Error: certificate verify failed: certificate has expired. First occurrence 09:11:47Z, sustained at 40-60 events per second.
checkout submit returns 502: checkout-api: POST /v2/checkout/submit returning 502 upstream_unavailable after payments-connector exhausted 3 retries. Correlated with payments-connector TLS failures.

checkout-api error ratio above objective: Alert checkout-api-error-ratio fired. Observed 5xx ratio 0.184 over a 5 minute window against an objective of 0.005. Affected route: POST /v2/checkout/submit. Alert remained firing until 09:58:10Z.

checkout-api latency objective burn: Alert checkout-api-latency fired. p99 latency for POST /v2/checkout/submit rose from 240ms to 10400ms. The 10400ms value sits at the configured client timeout, which is a ceiling rather than a measured completion time.

INC-7742 opened: INC-7742 opened at 09:15:00Z, severity 1, title 'Checkout submit failing for all customers'. Impact field left empty. No customer-impact estimate was recorded at any point during the incident.
responder attributes incident to the release: Responder A: 'We shipped 2026.5.14-a two minutes before this started. That is almost certainly the cause, let us roll it back.'

sampled failing checkout trace: Trace 5f21c0: POST /v2/checkout/submit total 10402ms. Span checkout.validate 12ms ok. Span payments.authorize 10388ms error, terminated by client timeout, no upstream response recorded. No span entered the email template or CSV export code paths.

responder disputes the release attribution: Responder B: 'The release only touched email templates and the CSV export dependency. Nothing in it is on the submit path. The connector logs show expired-certificate TLS failures starting at 09:11:47Z, which is before the alert but after the deploy. I think we are looking at the payments gateway certificate.'
payments connector recovers: checkout-api payments-connector: outbound TLS handshakes to payments-gateway.internal:8443 succeeding again. Error rate returned to baseline at 09:57:55Z.

gateway team reports certificate rotation: Responder C from the payments-gateway team: 'Our leaf certificate for payments-gateway.internal expired at 09:11:40Z. We rotated it and it took effect at 09:57:50Z. We have no record of who owns the renewal automation for that host.'

checkout-api rollback to 2026.5.13-c: Rollback of checkout-api to 2026.5.13-c completed at 10:04:18Z. The 5xx ratio had already returned to 0.004 at 09:58:10Z, six minutes before this rollback completed.
INC-7742 resolution note: INC-7742 marked resolved. Resolution note reads only 'rolled back and recovered'. The note does not mention the certificate rotation reported in the incident channel.
